YouTube Bait: Are Lets Play Videos Encouraging Bad Games?
Bad games? A game is only bad if you don't have a good time playing it. If you are enjoying yourself, the game is doing its job.

My interest in a game has never been influenced by a Let's Play in a way that led me to buy it and then realize after that it was shit. I don't need to buy Surgeon Simulator, Goat Simulator, or I Am Bread to know that I would not enjoy them. But that doesn't mean they're bad games. It means they don't personally interest me.

And frankly, if a person is in the habit of buying bad games because they saw them on a Let's Play and their enthusiasm for the host got them hyped up over nothing, then that's a lesson for the consumer to make decisions on their own without letting others influence them so heavily. If you want to be the kind of person who goes through life as easy prey for salespeople and schlockmeisters, then buy all means abandon your own good judgement and spend your hard earned money after someone else has done your thinking for you. I do my own thinking. It involves more effort but a lot less regret.

I would rather argue that Lets Play Videos encourage the development of games that are boring to play by yourself but can be mildly interesting if you watch someone else play them, with the recurring issue being lack of replay value and low production quality. The point is that most people watching Lets Play vids typically are not even that particularly interested in the game itself but want to see the reaction and the antics of the respective entertainer.

Case in point: Many of the most popular Lets Play videos focus on poking fun at how bad or buggy certain games are.

I wouldn't put FNAF in there, considering that even though those games have plenty of youtube-serving jumpscares, they are properly built horror games that deliver the intended experience when played. The fun isn't to go around in the game and poke at it to find "bugs".

I don't think Let's Plays are making games worse as a whole. Only an incredibly small amount of games are designed in this way, and they are reaching saturation already (see how bad the newer ones are doing). What does happen with Let's Plays is actually the reverse of that, in a sense. Games that have very little gameplay value or choices offer basically the same experience when played and when watched, which leads to lower sales. A couple of devs have already complained about this but honestly I don't really give a damn if the game doesn't have interesting gameplay.
